entries.clue: Sleep with CIA operative, being particular (8)

indicatorNotes.operative: operative means working, so the letters are put to work in a new order

annotation.surface: A spy is told to seduce a target for the CIA.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Operative' reads as a noun, a CIA agent, but it is working as an adjective telling you to rework SLEEP and CIA.
annotation.definitionFit: Especial is a formal word for particular or special, as in 'of especial interest'.

entries.clue: Prevent a stiff one from breaking down (6)

annotation.definition: Prevent a stiff one from breaking down

blocks.note: the surface offers a strong drink; the meant reading is a stiff, slang for a corpse
the surface offers an emotional collapse; the meant reading is a body decomposing

annotation.surface: Someone tries to stop a stiff drink or a nervous person from cracking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A stiff one' suggests a strong drink and 'breaking down' an emotional collapse; read 'stiff' as a corpse and 'breaking down' as decay.
annotation.definitionFit: To embalm a body is to treat it with preservatives so it does not decompose.

entries.clue: Political enforcer needs to celebrate with joint (5,4)

blocks.note: the hip is a joint of the body

annotation.surface: A parliamentary heavy has to unwind by getting stoned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joint' plays on a cannabis cigarette, but here it is a body joint. A party whip is the MP who makes colleagues vote the party line.
annotation.definitionFit: A party whip is the official who keeps a party's MPs in line and voting as instructed.

entries.clue: Do the same as jailbird with "previous" (7)

blocks.note: 'previous' and 'form' are both British slang for a criminal record; 'with' joins them

annotation.surface: Someone is urged to follow the example of a convict with a record.
annotation.walkthrough: In British slang a criminal 'has previous' or 'has form', meaning earlier convictions, which is why the quotation marks sit round 'previous'.
annotation.definitionFit: To conform is to do the same as everyone else, following the accepted pattern.

entries.clue: Minister without Portfolio's chief offence (5)

indicatorNotes.without: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away
indicatorNotes.chief: chief means head, so only the first letter of Portfolio is meant

blocks.note: a parson is a minister of the church
the first letter of Portfolio, removed from PARSON

annotation.surface: A government minister with no department commits some crime.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Minister without Portfolio' is a real cabinet title, which glues the words together; split it and the minister is a clergyman.
annotation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

entries.clue: A feature of Dolly's entertainment venue (3,3)

blocks.note: Dolly Parton is famous for her large bust, so a generously sized garment for the upper body
the main tent of a circus

annotation.surface: Someone describes Dolly Parton's theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: Dolly is the country singer Dolly Parton, whose bust is her best-known feature; the 's lets the clue read as one phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: The big top is the main tent of a circus, where the show is staged.

entries.clue: Trendy business of copulation without head is not quite right (7)

indicatorNotes.without head: without its head, a phrase loses its first letter

blocks.note: the business of copulation is the sex act
SEX ACT loses its first letter S

annotation.surface: Someone complains that the fashionable sex industry is not quite right.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Business' suggests commerce, but 'business of copulation' is just a roundabout way to say SEX ACT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the prefix in- negates exact, and 'not quite right' is a softened way of saying imprecise.

entries.clue: Allure of casual theft, ultimately (5)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so take the last letter

blocks.note: a casual worker is a temp

annotation.surface: Someone muses on the thrill of opportunistic stealing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Casual' looks like an adjective describing theft, but it is a noun: a casual is a temporary worker.
annotation.definitionFit: To allure is to tempt, drawing someone in with an attraction.

entries.clue: Secure member's irritation (3,5)

blocks.note: member and prick are both slang for the penis; the 's is has, joining the pieces

annotation.surface: Someone has a sore spot on their private parts.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a medical complaint about a penis; the word 'member' supplies PRICK.
annotation.definitionFit: A pinprick is a small annoyance, a minor irritation.

entries.clue: Utensil, brass, associated with sleep over (8)

indicatorNotes.over: over means turned over, so the word goes backwards

blocks.note: brass and sauce both mean cheek, impudence
a nap is a short sleep

annotation.surface: A brass kitchen tool is somehow connected with a night's rest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brass' looks like the metal a utensil is made of, but it is British slang for nerve or cheek, like 'sauce'.
annotation.definitionFit: A saucepan is a cooking pot, a kitchen utensil.

entries.clue: Aristocrat needs to stop working! (5)

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working

annotation.surface: A jibe that the idle rich should quit their jobs, as if they had any.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stop working' reads as one instruction; split it into two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the baron is the lowest rank of the British peerage, one kind of titled noble.

entries.clue: Trump's unlikely to be seen as this guy from the US? (9)

annotation.definition: Trump's unlikely to be seen as this

blocks.clueFragment: Trump's unlikely to be seen as this
blocks.note: a wise, respected political leader, which Trump's critics say he is not
the US is the States, and a guy is a man; split the word in two

annotation.surface: A dig at Trump's reputation abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word: a STATES MAN is a man from the United States, which Trump certainly is.
annotation.definitionFit: A statesman is a skilled, respected political leader, a title critics would deny Trump.

entries.clue: Sex partner getting depressed? Give up! (3,4)

blocks.note: a lay is slang for a sexual partner

annotation.surface: A lover feels low and is told to stop trying.
annotation.walkthrough: To give up is to lay down, as in laying down your arms or laying down a claim.
annotation.definitionFit: To lay down arms or a position is to surrender it, to give it up.

entries.clue: Hire husband to probe ex-president (7)

indicatorNotes.to probe: a probe goes inside something, so H goes into the name

blocks.note: h = husband, the abbreviation from family trees

annotation.surface: An investigator is hired to dig into a former president.
annotation.walkthrough: Jimmy Carter was US president from 1977 to 1981. 'Probe' makes the surface sound like an investigation, but it only means going inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialised synonym: hiring a whole vehicle, such as a yacht, coach or plane, for your own group's use.

entries.clue: Tom's having an erection, OK? (6,2)

blocks.note: Tom Thumb, the tiny folk-tale hero, so Tom's other name is THUMB'S

annotation.surface: A worried enquiry about whether Tom's performance is going well.
annotation.walkthrough: Tom Thumb is the thumb-sized boy of the English folk tale, so 'Tom's' stands for THUMB'S.
annotation.definitionFit: A thumbs up is a sign of approval, meaning OK.

entries.clue: Plan D to get into cryptic clues, eh? (8)

indicatorNotes.cryptic: cryptic means puzzling or obscured, so the letters are scrambled

annotation.surface: A setter decides Plan D is to put more into the cryptic clues.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue talks about itself: 'cryptic clues' sounds like the puzzle, but 'cryptic' is the instruction to rearrange D, CLUES and EH.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as noun or verb: a timetable of events, or to fix when something will happen.

entries.clue: Theme from 'Return of Historic, I POTUS' (5)

indicatorNotes.from: from means taken out of, so the letters lie inside the phrase
indicatorNotes.Return of: a return goes back, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: reversal indicator: the run is read backwards

annotation.surface: A headline about Trump coming back for a second term.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is Trump's historic return as POTUS, the US president; 'Return' is really the instruction to read the hidden letters backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the subject a talk or essay is about, from Greek for commonplaces.

entries.clue: Dicky, main one up for a complaint (9)

indicatorNotes.Dicky: dicky is British slang for faulty or unsound, so the letters are out of order

annotation.surface: A man called Dicky is got up to lodge a grievance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name, but it is British slang for weak or faulty, as in a dicky heart.
annotation.definitionFit: Pneumonia is a lung infection, and complaint is a common word for an illness.

entries.clue: Novel position on Mirror's lead press story (4,4)

indicatorNotes.lead: the lead is what comes first, so take the first letter

blocks.note: first letter of Mirror, placed on the end

annotation.surface: An editorial stance leads the Daily Mirror's coverage.
annotation.walkthrough: The Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper, which makes 'press story' blend into the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain equivalent: journalists call each separate piece in a bulletin or paper an item, and the press is the newspapers.

entries.clue: Bonking not started before half of pelvis put out (5)

indicatorNotes.not started: a word not started lacks its first letter

blocks.note: bonking is British slang for sex; SEX without its first letter
the first three of PELVIS's six letters

annotation.surface: Having sex is interrupted by a hip injury.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bonking' is British slang for having sex, so it stands for SEX before the first letter goes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from Latin for driving out, used of pupils ejected from school or air forced from the lungs.

entries.clue: Bog awful art in bar (7)

indicatorNotes.awful: awful means bad, so the letters are in a bad order
indicatorNotes.in: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: a bar or line, a straight stroke
ART rearranged, placed after the L of LINE

annotation.surface: A critic slams the ugly pictures on a pub wall as rubbish.
annotation.walkthrough: Bog is British slang for a toilet, not a marsh here. L(ATR)INE.
annotation.definitionFit: A latrine is a basic toilet, which bog means in British slang.

entries.clue: Biden-Trump's more helpful than Trump-Biden's (in faith and overtly)? (8)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the answer lies inside the phrase

blocks.note: surface padding: the joke comparing the two transfers of power

annotation.surface: A comparison of the two transfers of power between Biden and Trump.
annotation.walkthrough: Biden handing power to Trump in 2025 was smoother than Trump's grudging handover to Biden in 2021; the rest of the clue is that joke, and the answer hides in 'faith and overtly'.
annotation.definitionFit: Biden to Trump was a handover, a transfer of power from one president to the next.

entries.clue: Old empire's crappy motto gets to one (7)

indicatorNotes.crappy: crappy means bad, so the letters are mangled

annotation.surface: A former empire's feeble slogan finally gets through to someone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old empire's' is the definition plus 's, a way to join it to the rest of the sentence.
annotation.definitionFit: The Ottoman Empire ruled Turkey and much of the Middle East until 1922.

entries.clue: Long boring account about Republican covered in semen (6)

indicatorNotes.covered in: covered in puts one piece inside another

blocks.note: seed is an old word for semen; CR goes inside it

annotation.surface: A lurid, tedious report of a Republican sex scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: S(CR)EED: 'about' is not a container word here but the abbreviation c, for circa.
annotation.definitionFit: A screed is a long, tedious piece of writing or speech.

entries.clue: Eyes as they should be; audibly expressed relief "about time!" (7)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes the state of the eyes; sighted is the adjective for eyes that can see

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to sigh is to express relief with a breath you can hear

annotation.surface: Someone groans 'about time!' when their eyesight is finally sorted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Audibly' only describes the sigh; this is not a sound-alike clue. SIGH(T)ED.
annotation.definitionFit: Sighted means able to see, which is how eyes should be.

entries.clue: Delight in slating US today? (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the answer lies within the phrase

annotation.surface: Someone enjoys running down America these days.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals on US make it look like America, which disguises the run of letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty enjoyment, delight in doing something.

entries.clue: Too camp perhaps to be a natural feature of Washington (7)

indicatorNotes.perhaps: perhaps signals the letters could be another arrangement

annotation.surface: Someone is judged too flamboyant to fit in naturally in Washington politics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Natural feature' suggests a trait of character, which fits the camp surface; here it is geography.
annotation.definitionFit: The Potomac is the river that flows through Washington DC.

entries.clue: Post Office's, er, a vexed question (5)

annotation.surface: A hesitant spokesperson fields an awkward question about the Post Office.
annotation.walkthrough: The Post Office scandal, in which hundreds of British sub-postmasters were wrongly convicted, makes 'vexed question' fit the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a question that poses a real problem, one that leaves the listener stumped.

entries.clue: Check lice crawling on son's balls (9)

indicatorNotes.crawling: crawling suggests movement, so the letters shift about

annotation.surface: A parent is told to inspect a boy's groin for lice.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end and the surface is exactly about it, so the only work is spotting TEST and the scrambled LICE.
annotation.definitionFit: A slang equivalent: the round shape gives the vulgar word, which the surface's son and lice make literal.

entries.clue: Pie filling to produce rather strained movement? (5)

blocks.note: the sweet fruit mixture in a British Christmas pie, or ground meat
walk with short, dainty, affected steps

annotation.surface: A pie filling that brings on a hard time on the toilet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strained movement' suggests a bowel movement, but mincing is a dainty, affected way of walking.
annotation.definitionFit: Mince is minced meat or the fruit mixture in mince pies; to mince is to walk in a prissy way.

entries.clue: Idler who makes a cheeky gesture (6)

blocks.note: to moon about is to idle listlessly
to moon is to bare your buttocks

annotation.surface: A layabout is known for rude gestures.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheeky' has a second sense here: the gesture shows your cheeks, the buttocks.
annotation.definitionFit: A mooner idles or mopes about, and also flashes a bare bottom.

entries.clue: Doctor, new in UK – a short way to be an alcoholic? (8)

indicatorNotes.in: in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: n = new; it goes inside UK

annotation.surface: A doctor new to Britain finds a quick route to heavy drinking.
annotation.walkthrough: DR + U(N)K + A + RD. 'Short way' reads as a shortcut, but it is the abbreviation for road.
annotation.definitionFit: A drunkard is someone habitually drunk, an alcoholic.
